prompt.context: Our client is LAVA, a licensed distributor of Waterlogic water purifiers in Southeast Asia. They obtained exclusive rights to distribute water purifiers within the region 4 years ago. While they enjoyed huge growth in the past 3 years when they first entered the market, sales have slowed, and they are now in a loss-making position. Management has called us in to diagnose the key issues as well as turn the business around.
prompt.question: How would you advise them to proceed?

clarifying_info.q: Which geographies does LAVA operate in?

clarifying_info.a: B2C. The local sales team travels door to door to sell products and services. Products come with a 1-year warranty. LAVA also sells yearly service packages. The HQ team sits in Singapore and operates from a 10-person office.
Top-of-the-line water purifiers manufactured in the US. The product lineup has not changed in the past 4 years. Product life is about 5 years.
LAVA's closest competitor is Cuckoo Zater purifiers. Their technology is less advanced than LAVA's and they serve different markets.
To maximise profit. No specific time horizon or target amount has been given.

exhibits.title: Profits across geographies
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing annual profits (USD, implied thousands) for Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Vietnam from 2016 to 2019. LAVA only started operations in Malaysia and Vietnam in 2018.

exhibits.title: Gross profits for Thailand and Indonesia
exhibits.shows: A table showing volume sold (units) and gross margins (USD millions) for water purifiers and service packages in Thailand and Indonesia from 2016 to 2019. A footnote states gross profits are calculated net of COGS paid to Waterlogic, and that total estimated market size is 100,000 units for Thailand and 50,000 units for Indonesia.

exhibits.title: Thailand and Indonesia Cost Structure
exhibits.shows: Two stacked bar charts comparing cost structures in 2016 vs 2019 for Thailand and Indonesia, broken down into servicing costs, sales team salaries, sales team commissions, and HQ and other SG&A. A footnote states that 10% of gross margins are paid as sales team commissions.

framework: Revenue breakdown: (1) Number of customers x Spending per customer; two revenue streams — Water Purifier sales and Service Package sales

Revenue decline drivers: market saturation (4 years in market, product lineup unchanged), market crowded by competitors, customers switching to cheaper models, customers not buying service packages, distributorship contract becoming more restrictive
Cost breakdown: Fixed Costs (HQ/SG&A, sales team base salaries, servicing costs) and Variable Costs (sales team commissions tied to gross margin)
Cost increase drivers: sales team salaries risen, servicing costs risen, fixed cost base heavy relative to declining revenue

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1: Which markets are driving the profit decline and which show growth potential?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify Thailand and Indonesia as the key loss-making markets (both turned negative by 2019). Malaysia and Vietnam only started in 2018 and profits are not yet material, but represent potential growth. Candidate should prioritise diagnosing Thailand and Indonesia.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 2: What are the key insights about volume and margin trends in Thailand and Indonesia?
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers three points: (1) Purifier unit sales are declining steadily — Thailand down from 20k to 12k (40% drop), Indonesia down from 12k to 7k (~42% drop), suggesting market saturation given product lineup has not changed in 4 years; (2) Service package adoption is below cumulative installed base — by 2019 Thailand has ~65k cumulative purifiers sold but only 10k service packages, Indonesia ~42k purifiers but only 7.5k packages — meaning most customers are servicing elsewhere or not at all; (3) Gross margin per unit has stayed constant (purifier margin ~$1,000/unit throughout), so the problem is volume-driven, not margin-compression-driven. Candidate should compute market share: Thailand ~12k/100k = 12%, Indonesia ~7k/50k = 14%, confirming approaching saturation for a door-to-door B2C model.

math.setup: Compute margin per purifier unit to verify it is constant. Thailand 2019: $12.0M gross margin / 12,000 units = $1,000/unit. Thailand 2016: $20.0M / 20,000 = $1,000/unit. Same for Indonesia.
steps: Service package penetration vs installed base (Thailand by end 2019): cumulative purifiers sold = 20k+18k+15k+12k = 65k; service packages active = 10k; penetration ~15%
math.answer: Margin per unit is constant at $1,000/purifier and ~$200/service package. Volume is the only driver of decline. Service package penetration is very low (~15%) vs installed base — indicating a significant revenue leakage problem.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm: How can LAVA increase gross margins given what we know so far? (Interviewer should push until B2B is identified.)
Estimation: Estimate the gross margin uplift from expanding into the B2B market in Thailand in the first year.
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment businesses by size, apply % that have offices, estimate units needed per office, apply a realistic first-year capture rate, and multiply by $1,000 margin/unit. The suggested approach below is illustrative; any well-structured estimate with reasonable assumptions earns credit. Candidate should only count purifier sales (not service) for the near-term break-even objective.

math.setup: Segment Thailand businesses into Small, Medium, and Large. Estimate number of offices, units needed, % captured in year 1, and apply $1,000 margin/unit.
steps: Small businesses: 100,000 total x 50% have offices = 50,000 offices x 1 unit x 2% captured = 1,000 units x $1,000 = $1,000,000
Medium businesses: 20,000 total x 80% have offices = 16,000 offices x 2 units x 2% captured = 640 units x $1,000 = $640,000
Large businesses: 6,000 total x 100% have offices = 6,000 offices x 5 units x 1% captured = 300 units x $1,000 = $300,000
Total B2B margin uplift Thailand year 1: $1,000,000 + $640,000 + $300,000 = $1,940,000
math.answer: Approximately $1.94 million gross margin uplift from B2B expansion in Thailand in the first year.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 3: What does the cost structure reveal and what should LAVA do about it?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) The company is very fixed-cost heavy — sales team salaries are ~$11.5M in Thailand and ~$7M in Indonesia and have NOT changed between 2016 and 2019, even as gross margins fell ~30%; (2) Sales team commissions (variable component) have shrunk from $2.0M to $1.4M in Thailand and $1.2M to $0.9M in Indonesia, reflecting lower gross margins — commissions are only ~10% of gross margin, so the variable portion is tiny relative to fixed salaries; (3) The sales team is likely unmotivated because the vast majority of their compensation is fixed and unlinked to performance. Recommendation: variabilise sales team compensation by shifting more pay to commission/performance bonuses tied to revenue or profit.

math.setup: Verify sales team compensation split and decline in total costs vs gross margin decline.
steps: Thailand: gross margin dropped from $20M (2016) to $14M (2019) = -30%. Total costs dropped from $16M to $15.4M = -3.75%. Cost base barely moved.
Thailand salaries fixed at $11.5M both years. Commission fell $2.0M -> $1.4M (= 10% of GM). Fixed salary as % of total comp: 2016 = 11.5/(11.5+2.0) = 85%; 2019 = 11.5/(11.5+1.4) = 89%.
Indonesia: gross margin dropped from $12M to $8.5M = -29%. Total costs $9.5M -> $9.2M = -3%.
math.answer: Despite ~30% gross margin decline, total costs fell only ~4%. Fixed salaries are ~85-89% of total sales team compensation. The cost structure is dangerously fixed.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm ways LAVA can increase gross margins. Consider both revenue and cost levers.

categories.name: Increase number of customers — B2C
ideas: Educate customers on product quality differences vs cheaper Cuckoo alternatives to defend share
Introduce new product lines or updated models to re-stimulate B2C demand
Expand into Malaysia and Vietnam more aggressively as less saturated markets

categories.name: Increase number of customers — B2B (KEY)
ideas: Enter B2B channel selling to corporate offices, hotels, restaurants, co-working spaces
B2B customers need multiple units per site and represent an untapped segment
Estimated $1.94M GM uplift in Thailand year 1 from B2B expansion

categories.name: Increase spending per existing customer
ideas: Investigate why customers are not purchasing service packages (price? awareness? competitor services?)
Identify 'service poachers' — third parties servicing LAVA products at lower cost
Bundle service packages with purifier purchase at point of sale
Introduce premium product models with higher margins

categories.name: Reduce costs
ideas: Variabilise sales team compensation — shift from fixed salary heavy to commission-heavy structure tied to gross margin or revenue
Reduce fixed cost burden by right-sizing HQ given lower revenue
Negotiate better COGS terms with Waterlogic HQ given volume data
Explore whether servicing can be done more efficiently or outsourced

recommendation: LAVA's profit decline is driven by two compounding problems: (1) B2C market saturation in Thailand and Indonesia with a stale product lineup causing ~30-40% volume decline, and (2) a dangerously fixed cost structure where sales team salaries have not flexed with the revenue drop. To turn the business around, LAVA should pursue both revenue uplift and cost restructuring simultaneously.

Revenue: Expand into B2B in Thailand (est. $1.94M GM uplift year 1). Roll out similarly to Indonesia. Aggressively pursue service package sales to the large installed base (~65k units in Thailand alone). Explore product refresh to re-stimulate B2C demand and expand into Malaysia and Vietnam.
Cost: Variabilise sales team compensation — reduce fixed base and increase commission rate linked to gross margin performance to align incentives with company outcomes.
risks: Variabilising compensation may trigger sales team attrition or resistance; change management and communication of new scheme is critical
B2B channel requires different sales capabilities and go-to-market approach than current door-to-door B2C model
Service package revenue leakage may persist if root cause (price, awareness, third-party competition) is not investigated and addressed
next_steps: Investigate root cause of low service package take-up (survey customers, audit who is servicing the installed base)
Quantify B2B margin uplift for Indonesia using same estimation framework
Design new sales compensation structure and model the P&L impact
Replicate profitable elements of the Thailand/Indonesia model in Malaysia and Vietnam
